policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.48: Neuromuscular and Peroneal Nerve Electrical Stimulation (NMES)
source_section: Policy/Criteria - Section I NMES for Disuse Atrophy
source_quote: neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) is medically necessary when used as one component of a comprehensive rehab program for the treatment of disuse atrophy when the nerve supply to the atrophied muscle is intact and has any of the following atrophy indications: A. Contractures due to scarring of soft tissue (e.g., burn lesions); B. Previous casting or splinting of a limb; C. Major knee surgery with failure to respond to physical therapy; D. Recent hip replacement and NMES will be used until physical therapy begins.
clinical_service_or_procedure: Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation (NMES) for Disuse Atrophy (HCPCS E0745)

criteria.description: Part of a comprehensive rehabilitation program
Nerve supply to the atrophied muscle is intact
Atrophy indication: soft tissue contractures/burn, previous cast/splint, major knee surgery failed PT, or recent hip replacement

required_documentation: Neurologic exam confirming intact peripheral nerve supply
review_notes: Indicated as one component of comprehensive rehab for qualifying disuse atrophy.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.48: Neuromuscular and Peroneal Nerve Electrical Stimulation (NMES)
source_section: Policy/Criteria - Section II FES for Spinal Cord Injury
source_quote: functional electrical stimulation (FES) is medically necessary for spinal cord injury (SCI) when all of the following criteria are met: A. The member/enrollee has brisk muscle contraction to stimulation and sensory perception of electrical stimulation sufficient for muscle contraction; B. At least six months have passed since recovery from spinal cord injury and restorative surgery; C. Member/enrollee is highly motivated, committed, and has the cognitive ability to use FES devices for walking; D. Successful completion of a training program consisting of at least 32 physical therapy sessions with the device over a three-month period; E. Member/enrollee demonstrates a willingness to use the device long-term;
clinical_service_or_procedure: Functional Electrical Stimulation (FES) for Spinal Cord Injury (HCPCS E0764, E0770)

criteria.description: Brisk muscle contraction and sensory perception to stimulation
≥ 6 months post-recovery from SCI and restorative surgery
Completed training program of at least 32 PT sessions over 3 months
No contraindications: pacemaker, severe scoliosis/osteoporosis, skin disease/cancer, contracture, dysreflexia

required_documentation: Physical therapy log verifying ≥32 training sessions
review_notes: Mandatory 32-session training prerequisite and 6-month post-SCI stability.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.48: Neuromuscular and Peroneal Nerve Electrical Stimulation (NMES)
source_section: Policy/Criteria - Section IV Peroneal Nerve Non-Covered
source_quote: peroneal nerve stimulators (e.g., NESS L300, NESS L300 Plus, L300 Go System, WalkAide, Odstock [ODFS®] Dropped Foot Stimulator) have not been proven safe and effective for any indication other than incomplete spinal cord injury, including, but not limited to: foot drop in cerebral palsy, multiple sclerosis, traumatic brain injury, or stroke.
clinical_service_or_procedure: Peroneal nerve stimulators (WalkAide, NESS L300) for Non-SCI Indications

criteria.description: Foot drop due to cerebral palsy
Foot drop due to multiple sclerosis
Foot drop due to traumatic brain injury or stroke

review_notes: Peroneal nerve stimulators are unproven for non-incomplete SCI indications.
